profiles.summary: The mainnet node still reports tempo/v1.19.0-697ea97 and pins evm2 66687c18 with ruint 1.21.1. Two code paths in front of the interpreter were not read before: a process-wide cache in front of every KECCAK256 and a JIT compiler that the published binaries do not contain. Validators can run x86-64 or aarch64 builds, which take different jump destination and division code.

deltas.delta: The tempo binary enables the alloy-primitives feature keccak-cache-global by default, so the KECCAK256 opcode (evm2 crypto.rs calls alloy_primitives::keccak256) goes through a process-wide set associative cache of 131,072 buckets for inputs of 1 to 87 bytes. The cache key holds the input length and every input byte, equality compares both, and a bucket is read and written only while its tag is locked with an acquire compare and swap (fixed-cache 0.1.10). A hash collision only evicts an entry and cannot return another input's hash.

evm2 66687c18 ships an LLVM JIT (crates/jit). Tempo exposes it only through the opt-in cargo feature jit; the release workflow builds with --features asm-keccak,jemalloc,otlp plus the default features, and the Dockerfile with asm-keccak,jemalloc,otlp, so the published v1.19.0 binaries run the interpreter only.
deltas.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/697ea97/.github/workflows/release.yml (matrix features line 131, build line 174), https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/697ea97/Dockerfile, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/697ea97/crates/evm/Cargo.toml (jit feature line 103)

deltas.delta: Release binaries are built for x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu and aarch64-apple-darwin. On aarch64 the jump destination scan runs the NEON kernel (evm2 bytecode/analysis/aarch64.rs) and ruint 1.21.1 divides through the reciprocal path instead of the x86-64 div instruction (algorithms/div/small.rs div_nx1, div/reciprocal.rs reciprocal). The public endpoint reports x86_64, so mined blocks validated on aarch64 run code no probe on the endpoint reaches.

Tempo main pins evm2 35aa3280 (not on mainnet). Between 66687c18 and 35aa3280 the commits that touch execution are a one pass drain of transient storage for one address (ae1ebace, same result), trimming of pooled frame memory (8885390c, memory is still cleared on frame init), Host::execute_call for calls from outside a frame (2bc0eebb), and EIP-7702 and EIP-8037 refund and precompile warmth fixes. None changes an arithmetic, jump or hashing instruction.

cleared.check: Rerun of pmdiff.py (250 scripts) and pmdiff2.py (300 scripts) against Ethereum, and of swaps.py and replay.py on mined swaps.
cleared.result: Arc returned the same bytes as Ethereum for all 250 and all 300 scripts. Tempo matched 240 of 250 and 294 of 300, the same counts OPCODES.md records; pmdiff_explain.py shows the 10 pmdiff differences are 7 records cut short and 3 swaps that fail with empty return data, 8 of them identical with 20 times the gas, so they are the gas limit of a simulated call. Mined swaps: Tempo 946 with the tick relation exact for all and 210 pairs matching the single step formulas (208 exact input, 2 exact output); Arc 6,107 with 6,105 exact and 2 on a tick boundary, 5,818 pairs all explained, and all 14 multi step swaps replayed to the unit with up to 4 steps.

cleared.check: L-612: do all CPU-specific jump destination kernels of evm2 66687c18 (SSE4.1 with its 64 byte variant, AVX2, AVX-512 VBMI with its 128 byte variant, NEON with its 64 byte variant) give one jump destination set for the PoolManager runtime and for PUSH data holding 0x5b at every lane.
cleared.result: Yes. I read analysis.rs, analysis/x86.rs and analysis/aarch64.rs at 66687c18 and checked the lane transcription jd_sim.py against them (successor maps with bias 0x70 for the 16 byte kernels, unbiased 0..96 with vpermt2b exits for AVX-512, tbx keeping out of range lanes for NEON, the binary descent of 8, 4, 2 and 1 or 32 down to 2 steps plus one successor test, and the early returns for blocks without PUSH). All four kernels followed by the scalar tail equal the one-instruction-at-a-time rule on the 24,009 byte build and on the deployed Tempo runtime, each shifted by 0 to 127 leading bytes so every byte meets every lane (256 cases, 610 jump destinations), and on 28,014 constructed cases: PUSH32 at every offset 0 to 255 in buffers of 80, 160 and 300 bytes with 0x5b at each of its 32 data positions, every PUSHn in a buffer of 0x5b, and chains of PUSH32 with 0x5b data. A wrong scan would change which JUMP targets in the 709 constant jumps are valid; none differs.

cleared.check: Can the process-wide keccak cache in front of KECCAK256 on Tempo and Arc return a hash for the wrong input, which would move a pool id, position key, mapping slot or transient delta slot (src/libraries/Position.sol, src/types/PoolId.sol, src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol).
cleared.result: No. The key stores length and all bytes and equality compares both; inputs of 0 bytes and above 87 bytes bypass the cache; reads and writes hold the bucket lock through an acquire compare and swap and release on unlock, and a fresh bucket's zero key has length 0 and never equals a nonempty input. Vectors on both endpoints, sent three times in separate requests so later rounds meet cache hits: every length 1 to 96 at offsets 0, 1, 31, 32 and 33, pairs that differ only by one trailing zero byte, and zero inputs of every length, 766 vectors per round, all as specified. The PoolKey hash (160 bytes) bypasses the cache; the 64 byte mapping and delta slot inputs go through it.

cleared.check: Does the aarch64 build of Tempo compute DIV, MOD, MULMOD, ADDMOD, MUL, SHL and SAR the same as the x86-64 build, given that ruint 1.21.1 uses the x86-64 div instruction and _subborrow_u64 on x86-64 and the reciprocal and borrowing_sub fallback elsewhere.
cleared.result: Yes on 200 million cases. I built ruint 1.21.1 twice on x86-64, once unchanged and once with every target_arch = "x86_64" condition renamed so the fallback code compiles, and compared wrapping_div, wrapping_rem, mul_mod with a random and with the 2^256 - 1 modulus, add_mod, wrapping_mul, shift left and arithmetic shift right on operands built from zero, all ones, single bits, the top bit, near maximum limbs and shortened limb counts. No result differed, and the fallback quotient and remainder satisfied q*b + r = a with r < b in every case. This is the path FullMath.mulDiv and UnsafeMath.divRoundingUp take on an ARM validator.

cleared.check: Does evm2 66687c18 have other code that depends on the CPU or build flags in the instruction paths the PoolManager uses.
cleared.result: Only data movement. write_word, write_u64 and to_usize_opt in utils.rs and swap_words in stack.rs have AVX, AVX2 or AVX-512 variants selected by compile time target features, which the release build does not set, and each variant as read stores or tests the same four limbs as the plain one. signextend, i256_div, i256_mod and i256_cmp are plain limb code. The 0xef configurable account instruction and the millisecond timestamp instruction that Tempo adds are absent from the PoolManager runtime as an opcode (a linear disassembly finds no 0x4f, 0xef or 0x1e opcode; the two 0x5e are MCOPY).

cleared.check: Does reuse of pooled interpreter frames in evm2 leak memory or return data from an earlier frame into a later one, which would change what the PoolManager reads with MLOAD, RETURNDATACOPY or the call input it borrows.
cleared.result: No. Interpreter::init clears memory, sets return data to empty, the stack length to zero and the output range to empty before a pooled frame runs, and memory grows through Vec::resize with zero fill. The main branch commit 8885390c only bounds the capacity idle frames keep.

cleared.check: Does any ruint fix between 1.20.0, which Arc runs, and 1.21.1 correct a result an EVM instruction uses.
cleared.result: No. 1.20.1 adds shifts by primitive integers. The 1.21.0 fix list names div_3x2_ref, which in 1.20.0 is exported and tested but never called by division (grep of src: definition in algorithms/div/small.rs and a test only). The mul_mod fault fixed in 1.21.1 was introduced in 1.21.0. 1.20.0 itself contains the overflowing_shl and overflowing_shr flag fix that also corrected byte().

cleared.check: L-602: slot aliasing of storage and transient storage, and cross slot invariants of the PoolManager's committed storage, on Tempo and Arc.
cleared.result: No aliasing and no violation. slotalias.py and its transient variant wrote the caller into 22 base slots and read 5,837 related slots each (every XOR mask of one byte, neighbours across 128 boundaries, high bit flips and truncated page indices): all zero and the written slot read back on both networks. invariants.py on Tempo: 14 pools seen, 9 checked, 68 initialized ticks, 22,204 bitmap words, 18 eth_getStorageAt comparisons, 0 violations. On Arc: 194 seen, 186 checked, 994 ticks, 77,452 words, 106 comparisons, 0 violations. The bitmap and tick records that TickBitmap.flipTick and Pool.crossTick use are therefore stored where the source computes them.

cleared.check: Known weaknesses angle for Tempo: security releases and advisories of the last two years.
cleared.result: The changelog names one security release, v1.13.1, which patched alloy-core for decoder memory limits (a denial of service bound in ABI decoding); the v1.18.4 EVM execution fix was read in cycle 7 (L-197). A web search found no CVE or advisory for the Tempo node; results for the name concern Grafana Tempo. Neither release lets an ordinary account change what the PoolManager computes, and both are in v1.19.0.

cleared.check: Known weaknesses angle for Arc: advisories, audits and incident reports for arc-node.
cleared.result: None published. The changelog of v0.8.0 and v0.7.3 lists execution fixes for SELFDESTRUCT, block beneficiaries, EIP-161 deletion, withdrawals, a pending block RPC filter and denylist size checks, plus dependency advisories (h2). None is on a path the PoolManager executes; the PoolManager has no SELFDESTRUCT and makes no call that depends on the pending block filter.

leads.question: If alloy-primitives turns on fixed-cache LOCK_FREE_READS (new in fixed-cache 0.1.11) for the keccak cache, read the seqlock read path again: is the entry copy validated against a version that every writer bumps before and after writing.
leads.why: A torn read in that path would return a wrong KECCAK256 result for an input of 1 to 87 bytes, which covers the mapping and transient delta slots of the PoolManager.

leads.question: Repeat the fallback comparison for ruint 1.20.0 (x86-64 borrow chain versus borrowing_sub) and find out whether any Arc validator runs a non x86-64 build; my attempt to build the 1.20.0 harness was not permitted in this session.
leads.why: Arc has one client and a permissioned validator set whose hardware is not published.

leadResults.answer: All four kernel families of evm2 66687c18 give the reference jump destination set on the PoolManager runtime (build and deployed Tempo copy, 256 shifted cases) and on 28,014 PUSH data cases with 0x5b at every lane (raw/jd_l612.json). The published Tempo v1.19.0 binaries are built without the jit feature (release.yml features asm-keccak,jemalloc,otlp; jit is not a default feature of bin/tempo). Validators may run aarch64 builds, which use the NEON kernel, covered by the same transcription.

The arc/v1 label still names no commit. arc-node v0.8.0 and main have the same crates/evm/src/evm.rs and pins (revm 38.0.0, revm-interpreter 35.0.1, ruint 1.20.0), a public node reports reth/v2.2.0-508cbdf which matches the reth tag of v0.8.0, and the only replaced instruction is still SELFDESTRUCT in crates/evm/src/opcode.rs; the value-bearing frame checks in evm.rs are unchanged from the copy read in cycle 2. On the arc/v1 endpoint battery.py (99,985), targeted.py (85,544), pmdiff.py (250 of 250) and pmdiff2.py (300 of 300) all agree with the specification and Ethereum.

slotalias.py and a transient variant found no aliasing on Tempo or Arc (5,837 reads each), and invariants.py found 0 violations on 9 Tempo and 186 Arc pools. HyperEVM (999) belongs to another unit and was not run here.

crates.io lists 1.21.1 of 23 October 2026 as the newest ruint, with 1.21.0 yanked, on 24 November 2026. reth main and tempo main both pin ruint 1.21.1 in Cargo.lock. In addition the non x86-64 arithmetic paths of 1.21.1 agree with the x86-64 paths on 200 million cases (raw/ruint_fallback.log).
